newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends off sharply on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends off sharply on profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended sharply lower Tuesday in a moderately-active session, pressured by profit taking after Monday's rally amid forecasts for more moderate weather later next week, sources said.
February tumbled 30.2 cents to close at $3.334 per million British thermal units. March settled 17.9 cents lower at $3.026. Other months ended down by 1.5 to 9.4 cents.
"The rally was a bit overdone but I was surprised by the extent of the selloff. I guess some revised forecasts are saying the cold may not be that severe," said one East Coast trader.

While below-normal temperatures were still expected to dominate the Midwest and East this week, traders said some forecasters had moderated their outlook for the week and were calling for milder weather later next week.
"Some forecasters are calling for a warming trend next week," said a Texas trader, adding bearish estimates for Wednesday's AGA storage report also helped pressure the market today.
Early withdrawal estimates for the weekly inventory report ranged from 45 bcf to 120 bcf versus last year's decline of 138 bcf.
Technically, traders pegged February resistance in the $3.80-3.84 area, then in the $3.90s and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support remained in the $3.11-3.28 gap and then in the $2.60s.

In the physical market, Gulf Coast prices jumped Tuesday by more than 30 cents to the high-$3.70s. Midcon pipes were 20 cents higher in the mid-to-high $3.80s. New York city gate gas gained another 50 cents to about $4.50.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 8.1 cents to $2.459.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.
On the KCBT, February closed down 28.9 cents at $3.211, while deferreds finished steady to four cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 12.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
